newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds up, unaffected by political events.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds up, unaffected by political events.

text.p: Israeli bond prices continued to rise on Thursday unaffected by conflict with Palestinians with gains across the board except for dollar-linked bonds, traders said.
* Consumer price index (CPI) linked government bonds: +0.2 pct to 168.21
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 165.05
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 to 157.28

"The political events did not affect the market," said Adam Reuter, managing director of Financial Immunities, a financial and economic consultancy. "When the market decides merchandise is hot, nothing can affect it."

A two-day summit convened in Washington by President Bill Clinton achieved no concrete results. The summit was an attempt to defuse tensions between Israelis and Palestinians following bloody clashes that have killed 73 people since last week.
Reuter said prices of CPI-linked bonds were on the rise because provident funds had once again started to buy bonds and yields were still very attractive.
"Real gross yields for CPI-linked bonds up to two years are 4.5 percent, for two- to five-year bonds yields are at 4.7 percent and 4.8 percent for bonds up to 13 years," he said.
"Yields are still very high, even though in the last two days bond prices have gone back to the levels before the bond crisis in August," Reuter said.
Prices of dollar-linked bonds fell slighlty as a correction to gains the bonds had when the dollar strengthened earlier this week against the shekel, Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments said.

Notes: Provident funds, long-term savings funds with tax benefits, had been dumping bonds to meet massive public redemptions. To stop the falling bond prices the central bank has bought government bonds.
Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
